                    ### Question
                    A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motorcycle collision. He was not wearing a helmet. Physical examination shows left periorbital ecchymosis. A CT scan of the head shows a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. Physical examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Decreased sense of smell
opb. Numbness of the left cheek
opc. Preserved left lateral gaze
opd. Absent left corneal reflex
ope. Complete loss of vision of the left eye

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure is most likely to affect cranial nerves III, IV, V1, and VI. This can lead to numbness of the left cheek due to involvement of the ophthalmic branch (V1) of the trigeminal nerve, which is responsible for sensation in the forehead and upper part of the face, including the cheek. The involvement of cranial nerve VI (abducens nerve) could impair lateral gaze, but it is not certain if it would be preserved. The corneal reflex could be affected due to partial involvement of the trigeminal nerve (V1), but this is also uncertain. Complete loss of vision is unlikely as the optic nerve (CN II) is not typically involved in superior orbital fissure syndrome. Decreased sense of smell is unlikely as it involves the olfactory nerve (CN I), which is not affected by this type of fracture. Therefore, the most likely finding on physical examination is numbness of the left cheek.
